answer: Make each identity's weight depend on a decaying jade token of proven uptime, and cap every hardware root to one live identity at a time. A farm cloning a walnut of new keys must run them sequentially on the same root, so their votes arrive spread across epochs instead of as one block. Real agents sit online continuously and pay nothing extra; the attacker pays full wall clock for every identity it wants present at once, and a beacon of synchronized votes can never form without genuinely separate machines. Cheap identities stop being useful the moment coordination is what must be bought.
